scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports, from the 2026-11-22 file-level re-audit (method in structural-audit-2026-11-22.md).

findings.finding: Cost model version 1 is not transcreated: of `plan_cost_ver1.go`'s 40 functions only `getPlanCostVer1` for a few operators exists, so `SET tidb_cost_model_version = 1` costs and chooses plans differently (probe: `EXPLAIN FORMAT='verbose' SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE b > 1` costs 16279.11 in Go and 73382.22 in Rust; a two-table join on an indexed column is a HashJoin in Go and a MergeJoin in Rust).

`EXPLAIN EXPLORE <sql>` is answered as a plain EXPLAIN: Go's binding exploration (`ExplorePlansForSQL`, `getBindingPlanInfo`, `runToGetExecInfo`, `fillRecommendation`) and plan generation over hint states (`generatePlanWithSCtx`, `breadthFirstPlanSearch`, `genPlanUnderState`) have no Rust counterpart.
findings.rust_evidence: no module; the statement reaches the ordinary EXPLAIN path

findings.finding: ANALYZE is not in Go's shape. One 3,055-line `real_tikv_analyze.rs` holds the planner's `buildAnalyze*` / `getMustAnalyzedColumns`, the executor's `AnalyzeExec` and globalstats' async merge; Go's `AnalyzeExec` worker pool (`analyzeWorker`, `handleResultsError`, `handleGlobalStats`), `AnalyzeColumnsExec`'s sampling build (`buildSamplingStats`, `subMergeWorker`, `subBuildWorker`, `readDataAndSendTask`, `handleNDVForSpecialIndexes`), `analyze_idx.go`'s `fetchAnalyzeResult`, `analyze_global_stats.go` and `analyze_worker.go` have no counterparts.

Go's `SortExec.Open` always sorts in parallel (`IsUnparallel = false`, `ExecutorConcurrency` workers, multi-way merge, `parallelSortSpillHelper`), and TopN has its own workers; `parallel_sort_worker.go`, `parallel_sort_spill_helper.go` and `topn_worker.go` are not ported (the crate's own doc says so), so Rust sorts only in Go's unparallel mode.

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: `InferType4ControlFuncs` with its `setDecimalFromArgs` / `setFlenFromArgs` has two Rust implementations: `builtin_control.rs` (the function classes, with collation derivation) and `rewriter/control_type.rs` (LEAD/LAG's `typeInfer4LeadLag` and the windows' `set_numeric_len_from_args`, without it, plus per-function tails Go keeps in each `getFunction`). (Done 2026-11-22: the TiDB-store DAG goes through the one `ConstructDAGReq`, so `builder_utils.rs`'s second ToPB family (`AggFuncToPBExpr`, `AggFunctionModeToPB`, `GetTiPBExpr`, the table scan / selection / limit / TopN / aggregation / projection `ToPB`) is gone; one body each for `BoolToOnOff`, `CheckDropTablePartition`, `ContainCorrelatedColumn`, `ContainVirtualColumn`, `IsBinaryLiteral`, `base64NeededEncodedLength`, `newReturnFieldTypeForBaseBuiltinFunc`, `IsUpgradingClusterState`, `insertPlanReplayerStatus`, `isNullToNotNullChange`; the unused `Table::verify_no_overflow_shard_bits` is removed.)

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: Go's DDL `sess.Session` (`Execute`, `Begin`, `Commit`, `Rollback`) has two Rust ports: `tidb_ddl_session::Session` over a session context, and the `StepSqlSession` trait (with its own `execute`, `begin`, ...) that job steps hold, so code that runs on either is written twice (`getJobsBySQL` in `ddl_history.rs` and in `job_control.rs`).
